hints: Form equations of motion for particle $A$ ($T = m_A a$) and hanging particle $B$ ($m_B g - T = m_B a$).
Add the equations to find common acceleration $a$.
Use $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u = 0$ and $s = 2.5\text{ m}$ to find the time $t$.
walkthrough:
Set up Newton's second law equations of motion for both particles:
For particle $A$ on the smooth horizontal table:
$$T = m_A a = 0.8a$$
For hanging particle $B$ downwards:
$$m_B g - T = m_B a \implies 0.2(10) - T = 0.2a \implies 2 - T = 0.2a$$

Add both equations together to eliminate the tension $T$ and find the acceleration:
$$2 = (0.8 + 0.2)a \implies 2 = 1.0a \implies a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply the SUVAT displacement formula $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ starting from rest ($u = 0$):
$$2.5 = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(2)t^2 \implies t^2 = 2.5 \implies t = \sqrt{2.5} = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{2} \approx 1.58\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Set up Newton's second law for both connected particles:
For particle $A$ ($0.8\text{ kg}$) on the smooth table: tension $T$ is the only horizontal force:
$$T = 0.8a$$
For particle $B$ ($0.2\text{ kg}$) hanging freely: weight pulls down and tension pulls up:
$$0.2(10) - T = 0.2a \implies 2 - T = 0.2a$$

Add both equations together to eliminate tension $T$:
$$(T) + (2 - T) = 0.8a + 0.2a \implies 2 = 1.0a \implies a = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Particle $A$ starts from rest ($u = 0$) and covers distance $s = 2.5\text{ m}$. Use the displacement formula $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$:
$$2.5 = (0)(t) + \frac{1}{2}(2)t^2$$

Simplify the equation and take the square root to solve for time $t$:
$$2.5 = t^2 \implies t = \sqrt{2.5} \approx 1.58\text{ seconds}$$

hints: Find normal reaction $R = m_A g = 8\text{ N}$ and friction $F = \mu R = 0.1 \times 8 = 0.8\text{ N}$ on $A$.
Set up the equations of motion with friction: for $A$, $T - 0.8 = 0.8a$; for $B$, $2 - T = 0.2a$.
Solve for $a$, then use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $s = 2.5\text{ m}$ to find $v$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the frictional force opposing particle $A$'s motion on the rough table:
$$R = m_A g = 0.8(10) = 8\text{ N}$$
$$F = \mu R = 0.1 \times 8 = 0.8\text{ N}$$

Form the equations of motion for both connected particles:
For particle $A$: $T - F = m_A a \implies T - 0.8 = 0.8a$
For particle $B$: $m_B g - T = m_B a \implies 2 - T = 0.2a$
Adding the equations gives:
$$2 - 0.8 = (0.8 + 0.2)a \implies 1.2 = 1.0a \implies a = 1.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use the SUVAT relation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with initial speed $u = 0$ over distance $s = 2.5\text{ m}$:
$$v^2 = 0 + 2(1.2)(2.5) = 6 \implies v = \sqrt{6} \approx 2.45\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Now the table has friction ($\mu = 0.1$). First calculate the normal reaction on particle $A$ ($R = mg$):
$$R = 0.8 \times 10 = 8\text{ N}$$

Calculate the friction force opposing particle $A$ using $F = \mu R$:
$$F = 0.1 \times 8 = 0.8\text{ N}$$

Set up the new equations of motion:
For particle $A$: $T - 0.8 = 0.8a$
For particle $B$: $2 - T = 0.2a$

Add both equations together to eliminate $T$ and solve for the new acceleration $a$:
$$(T - 0.8) + (2 - T) = 0.8a + 0.2a \implies 1.2 = 1.0a \implies a = 1.2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use the SUVAT equation $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0$, $a = 1.2$, and $s = 2.5\text{ m}$ to find speed when hitting the pulley:
$$v^2 = 0^2 + 2(1.2)(2.5) = 2.4 \times 2.5 = 6$$

Take the positive square root to get the final velocity:
$$v = \sqrt{6} \approx 2.45\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
